title: NSA 2005 Release: The Gulf of Tonkin Deception
summary: On Dec 1, 2005 NSA declassified 140+ formerly top-secret documents including historian Robert J. Hanyok's SIGINT study. Conclusion: the Aug 2, 1964 engagement (USS Maddox) was real; the Aug 4, 1964 second attack did NOT happen — it rested on bad naval intelligence and misrepresented SIGINT. The Aug 4 incident was the basis for the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution (Aug 7, 1964) authorizing the war.
tldr: On December 1, 2005, the NSA declassified 140+ top-secret documents including historian Robert J. Hanyok's SIGINT study, which concluded the August 2, 1964 clash with the USS Maddox was real — but the August 4 'second attack' that justified the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution never happened.
ai_summary:
AI review of the National Security Archive's Electronic Briefing Book No. 132 press release on the NSA's December 1, 2005 declassification, read in full:
- The release covered 'over 140 formerly top secret documents' — histories, chronologies, SIGINT reports, and oral-history interviews on the August 1964 Gulf of Tonkin incident.
- Centerpiece: NSA historian Robert J. Hanyok's 'Skunks, Bogies, Silent Hounds, and the Flying Fish: The Gulf of Tonkin Mystery, 2-4 August 1964' (from the classified Cryptologic Quarterly, early 2001), arguing the SIGINT confirms the August 2 attack on the USS Maddox 'although under questionable circumstances,' while the August 4 attack 'did not occur despite claims to the contrary by the Johnson administration.'
- Hanyok charges agency officials 'mishandled' the August 4 SIGINT and gave top officials 'skewed' intelligence — 'the overwhelming body of reports, if used, would have told the story that no attack occurred' — and suggests 'an active effort to make SIGINT fit the claim,' though he found no 'smoking gun' of a cover-up.
- The declassification came after FOIA requester Matthew M. Aid (April 2004 request) and NYT reporting (Scott Shane, October 31, 2005) exposed senior NSA officials blocking release for fear of 'uncomfortable comparisons with the flawed intelligence used to justify the war in Iraq.'
- Record summary verified accurate against the document.
